content:
Communication is an essential part of our life. We need to communicate in different ways to meet our needs. Communication is something that we do in our day-to-day life. Speaking, writing, listening, etc. are different forms of everyday communications  . But the thing is that’s not everything. If you think only these are the communications, you have just ignored a large part of communication. That is the non-verbal communication. Casper Academy of Excellence is the best IELTS training centre in Kochi to give best coaching to secure high band score.

It is important to learn how to boost your performance in the IELTS exam. Knowing certain things can really help you in scoring well. Here you will learn how to incorporate whatever you learn for IELTS preparation in the non-verbal format. You can enhance your IELTS speaking score one step a time.

How to Use Non-verbal Communication to Score More?

Are you aware that more than 90% of you communication is not verbal or written? Most of you might not have. We express much through our body, gestures and expressions. Casper Academy of Excellence is giving best IELTS Coaching in Kochi with best faculties and infrastructure facilities. Here we will let you know, how to improve your skills. We can train ourselves with pre-planned answers, but the reactions that come while we react are natural. For this you have to learn how your body communicates even when you are unaware.

  • Head – You must keep your head upright and must not be drooping over your shoulders. Your head should face the examiner at a normal angle. Don’t hold your head too high or low. It might indicate certain other factors. You must keep your facial expression normal.
  • Eyes – You must maintain a good level of eye contact. Look at the examiner in the eye. Looking and speaking in the eye shows confidence, sincerity and credibility. This will make the discussions with the examiner to be more engaging. It could give a positive response to the examiner about you.
  • Mouth – Whatever you do, don’t frown. You can smile, but don’t overdo it. While you are speaking, speak firmly, clearly and in an average speed which is understood by the examiner. When you speak, the examiner must distinctly be able to identify and understand each word you speak. Also, you must not fake your accent.
  • Hand – It starts with greeting the examiner with a firm handshake. This is vital as it could make your first impression. It shows your confidence and emotional level in people. Don’t fold your arms and sit. Don’t touch your face while answering questions. You must emphasize what you want to say with hand gestures.
  • Legs – Don’t sit with your legs crossed. You must sit straight with your legs in a relaxed position along with your toes pointing towards the examiner. Don’t rub your legs or tap them on floor. Sit firmly.
  • Back – Keep your posture straight. As emotions can be detected via posture, this is important.
  • Breathing – Patterns of breathing depicts a person’s state of mind and mood. There is actually a direct relationship with breathing and body language. Excessive breathing shows anxiety or fear. Proper breathing will help you feel relaxed and more confident. You will learn to present yourself better with best IELTS coaching in Ernakulam, as from the Casper Academy of Excellence.
